messages.subject: R App works well Locally but doesn't get Published in shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: R App works well Locally but doesn't get Published in shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have created an app, the code for which is present at the end of this question. It works very well locally. The issue is when I try to publish it via shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and am unable to do so. I created an account on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and got the code with the token and secret, and connected my RStudio to it. When I try to publish the app the following error appears:

Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading bundle for application: 371701...Error: Unable to retrieve package records for the following packages:
- "GLMMGibbs", "a", "exNSS4", "graph", "myTst", "pkgA", "yags"
In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
Execution halted

I have tried many things, but it persists. Please do help me with the same. If I need to update or upgrade anything, I'll be glad to. Just need it to work.

The code of the app is:

library(tau)
library(data.table)
library(tm)
library(class)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(NLP)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(shiny)
library(packrat)

if (interactive()) {

  ui <- fluidPage(
    textAreaInput("resumehtml","Resume",width = 800,height=200),
    textAreaInput("jdhtml","Job Description",width = 800,height=200),
    actionButton("add", "Add"),
    h3(textOutput("another")),
    dataTableOutput("value")
  )
  server <- function(input, output,session) {
    observeEvent(input$add, {
    jd <- as.character(input$jdhtml)
    resume <- as.character(input$resumehtml)

    jd <- str_replace_all(jd, "[^[:alnum:]]", " ")
    jd.text <- iconv(jd,"ASCII")
    jd.corpus <- Corpus(VectorSource(jd.text))
    term.doc.matrix <- TermDocumentMatrix(jd.corpus,control=list(removePunctuation = TRUE, stopwords=c('for','in','the','on','of','com','with','oyo','Job Description','Job',stopwords('english')),removeNumbers=TRUE,tolower=TRUE))
    term.doc.matrix <- as.matrix(term.doc.matrix)
    word.freq <- sort(rowSums(term.doc.matrix),decreasing=T)
    dm <- data.frame(word=names(word.freq),freq=word.freq)

    resume <- str_replace_all(resume, "[^[:alnum:]]", " ")
    resume.text <- iconv(resume,"ASCII")
    resume.corpus <- Corpus(VectorSource(resume.text))
    term.doc.resume <- TermDocumentMatrix(resume.corpus,control=list(removePunctuation = TRUE, stopwords=c('Job Description','Job',stopwords('english')),removeNumbers=TRUE,tolower=TRUE))
    term.doc.resume <- as.matrix(term.doc.resume)
    word.freq.resume <- sort(rowSums(term.doc.resume),decreasing=T)
    dm.resume <- data.frame(word=names(word.freq.resume),freq=word.freq.resume)

    rm_words <- function(string, words) {
      stopifnot(is.character(string), is.character(words))
      spltted <- strsplit(string, " ", fixed = TRUE)
      vapply(spltted, function(x) paste(x[!tolower(x) %in% words], collapse = " "), character(1))
    }
    robbie <- rm_words(jd.text, tm::stopwords("en"))

    createNgram <-function(stringVector, ngramSize){

      ngram <- data.table()

      ng <- textcnt(stringVector, method = "string", n=ngramSize, tolower = FALSE)

      if(ngramSize==1){
        ngram <- data.table(w1 = names(ng), freq = unclass(ng), length=nchar(names(ng)))
      }
      else {
        ngram <- data.table(w1w2 = names(ng), freq = unclass(ng), length=nchar(names(ng)))
      }
      return(ngram)
    }

    jd.m2 <- createNgram(robbie,2)
    resume.multiple <- createNgram(resume.text,2)
    jd.m22 <- createNgram(jd.text,2)
    jd.m222 = merge(jd.m2[, c("w1w2", "freq")],
                    jd.m22[, c("w1w2", "freq")])

    jd.m3 <- createNgram(robbie,3)
    resume.m3 <- createNgram(resume.text,3)
    jd.m33 <- createNgram(jd.text,3)
    jd.m333 = merge(jd.m3[, c("w1w2", "freq")],
                    jd.m33[, c("w1w2", "freq")])

    final.jd1 <- dm[dm$freq>1,]
    final.jd2 <- jd.m222[jd.m222$freq>1,]
    colnames(final.jd2)[which(names(final.jd2) == "w1w2")] <- "word"
    final.jd3 <- jd.m333[jd.m333$freq>1,]
    colnames(final.jd3)[which(names(final.jd3) == "w1w2")] <- "word"
    final.jd <- rbind(final.jd1,final.jd2,final.jd3,fill=T)

    colnames(resume.multiple)[which(names(resume.multiple) == "w1w2")] <- "word"
    colnames(resume.m3)[which(names(resume.m3) == "w1w2")] <- "word"
    final.resume <- rbind(dm.resume,resume.multiple,resume.m3,fill=T)

    left_join <- merge(x = final.jd, y = final.resume, by = "word", all.x = TRUE)
    left_join[is.na <http://is.na>(left_join)] <- 'Not in Resume'
    colnames(left_join)[which(names(left_join) == "word")] <- "Keyword"
    colnames(left_join)[which(names(left_join) == "freq.x")] <- "Frequency in JD"
    colnames(left_join)[which(names(left_join) == "freq.y")] <- "Frequency in Resume"

    jinga <- nrow(left_join[left_join$`Frequency in Resume` == "Not in Resume",])
    totaljinga <- nrow(left_join)
    diffjinga <- totaljinga - jinga
    percjinga <- diffjinga/totaljinga
    fitscore <- round(percjinga * 100)

    output$another <- renderText({ paste("FIT SCORE (Match between your Resume and the JD):",fitscore) })

    output$value <- renderDataTable(left_join[,1:3])
    })
  }

   shinyApp(ui,server)
  }

messages.subject: Re: Loading precomputed Plotly Plots.
messages.subject_clean: Loading precomputed Plotly Plots.
messages.body_plain:
Found the solution. You were right, it seems like the creators of plotly or htmlwidgets are using absolute file paths for their dependencies. If "plot" is the name of the plot generated from plot_ly(), as an example, plot$dependancies[[1]]$src$file has a dependency defined by an absolute file path such as /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/library/plotly/htmlwidgets/lib/typedarray  on my mac. To make it work I changed this to /opt/R/3.3.2/lib/R/library/plotly/htmlwidgets/lib/typedarray a path on the shiny io server which works.

On Friday, July 6, 2018 at 9:41:18 AM UTC-4, Akash Sadashivapeth wrote:
> Oh sorry. I understand what you are saying. I better check if the objects stored in the RDS are referencing some local path. Thanks!
>
> On Friday, July 6, 2018 at 9:39:48 AM UTC-4, Akash Sadashivapeth wrote:
> > Strange because after I load the object I check if the variables exist and log the output. This shows me that the RDS is read successfully and all the stored variables exist. The error is only when i'm trying to work with the variables stored in the RDS.
> >
> >
> >
> > On Friday, July 6, 2018 at 9:01:47 AM UTC-4, Joshua Spiewak wrote:
> > > Well, that path looks to be Mac specific, which indicates to me that the path is being stored in the RDS file, and when you attempt to load that on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, that path won't work because it is not your local computer.
> > >
> > > On Thursday, July 5, 2018 at 8:46:50 PM UTC-4, Akash Sadashivapeth wrote:
> > > > I have saved a couple of plotly plots in a .RDS file and am reading it in on shiny. The system works perfectly fine locally, however, shinyio is throwing the following error:

messages.subject: My big shiny app runs very well locally in IE11, but very slow when deploying it to the shinyapps.io in IE11!!
messages.subject_clean: My big shiny app runs very well locally in IE11, but very slow when deploying it to the shinyapps.io in IE11!!
messages.body_plain:
Hi! I have a big app running very well locally, but when I deploy it to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> it runs very slowly in IE11. The page takes few seconds to load and there is a latency in render functions. This is not the same case in chrome. In chrome it works very well locally and when deploying it too. I want to make my app run better in IE11 when deploying it, how can I do that? what are the reasons behind the loading page latency in IE11?

Thank you for your support!
Best Regards,
Karni

messages.body_plain:
Correct, it appears that ggforce has an undeclared system dependency upon libudunits that can be worked around by including the R package udunits2, but really calls for an installer in shinyapps-package-dependencies <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies> per documentation <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/getting-started.html#system-packages>.

messages.subject: Re: My big shiny app runs very well locally in IE11, but very slow when deploying it to the shinyapps.io in IE11!!
messages.subject_clean: My big shiny app runs very well locally in IE11, but very slow when deploying it to the shinyapps.io in IE11!!
messages.body_plain:
Without knowing what you mean by big, or what your application is doing, I would suggest posting to the Shiny Community <https://community.rstudio.com/c/shiny> to reach a broader audience of Shiny users.

If IE11 has a developer console in which you can view the network traffic of requests, you might see what is going slowly from the browser's perspective.

Our organization is considering purchasing the professional version of shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, but have a few questions.

2) If we use a custom domain, https:// security disappears. Would we able to place a certification and maintain the application's functionality?

3) In the event that the servers hosting our application goes down, what is the time frame for expected turnaround?

4) Lastly, if we exceed 10,000 hours per month, what would overage charges look like? Can we buy 2 professional packages (10,000 hours per month) packages and apply it to the same account?

Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: Professional version of shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: Professional version of shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
1) Yes you will. We do not currently offer a branded authentication experience.

2) With a custom domain, the outer page is not fetched with HTTPS, that is correct. However, that page contains an inner iframe that is loaded over HTTPS. You are certainly welcome to host your own proxy server with an SSL certificate you manage. We do have it on our roadmap to use LetsEncrypt to generate certificates for custom domains, but no timeframe to convey at this time.

3) There is no SLA covering shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, but we monitor the servers and have an on-call rotation and maintain a status page <https://status.rstudio.com/>.

4) While we reserve the right to begin charging overages for exceeding hours, we are currently not doing so. Should that change, there will be plenty of notice communicated.

messages.body_plain:
My guess is that one of the packages you are using has an optional dependency upon the "markdown" package, and your code is triggering that code path.
We don't install optional packages, so if you need to make use of "markdown", add a call to "library(markdown)" in your code and redeploy.

messages.subject: Run exe file through Shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: Run exe file through Shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
First I start with my goal: I have an exe file which gets a data file, then does some computations and return an output files. I want to use R Shiny to get the input data from users, and then run the exe file and finally plot the results.

I used system() command and was able to get input from user and run the exe file, when I execute it locally on my PC. But, when I publish it online (in my Shinyapps.io account) it does not work. I checked the log in my account and got this msg:

sh: 1: foo.exe: not found
Warning in system("foo.exe") : error in running command

Is there a solution for what I am trying to do?

Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: Run exe file through Shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: Run exe file through Shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is a Linux environment, an exe file cannot run there.

That said, the fact that it couldn't be found might be due to it not being included in the bundle when deploying the application, Make sure all the files you want deployed are checked when you are prompted with the dialog when hitting the Publish button.

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to deploy R rest API on shinyapps.io?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to deploy R rest API on shinyapps.io?
messages.body_plain:
While it may be currently possible to deploy a plumber application to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, the application lifecycle <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/applications.html#application-life-cycle> may result in undesired behavior.

Official support for hosting R based APIs is on our roadmap, but we do not have a timeframe to share now.

On Wednesday, July 25, 2018 at 5:17:40 AM UTC-4, Antoine Tixier wrote:
> Can shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> be used as an equivalent of heroku for R? There are frameworks like flask for R (plumber or jug) which make it easy to expose R code as API. But can it be deployed to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>? It seems it's possible to deploy R to heroku ([link <https://github.com/virtualstaticvoid/heroku-buildpack-r>]), but since I'm already paying $1.1K/year for a shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> account and I know heroku is not free either, I thought I'd double check first :)

messages.body_plain:
I am hoping to link to a Shiny app I constructed in a paper. I am hoping to use a link that does not expire. Right now, I am simply typing a https URL like the following (https://userName.shinyapps.io/appName) into my paper.

However, will this link expire? If so, is there a suggested method to provide a link to an app that will not (or be less likely to) expire? Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: Permanent link to Shiny app
messages.subject_clean: Permanent link to Shiny app
messages.body_plain:
There is nothing about that link intrinsically that has an expiration.

However, should you desire more control and a layer of indirection, you could look into a URL shortening service such as bitly <https://bitly.com/> or Rebrandly <https://www.rebrandly.com/pricing>.

messages.body_plain:
Hello shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> users,

With the launch last year of the RStudio Community site <https://community.rstudio.com/> and its successful growth in participation over the past months, the time has come to close down this Google Group and shift new questions to the Community.

Please begin posting in the Shiny category <https://community.rstudio.com/c/shiny>. For questions about shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, please add the tag "shinyappsio <https://community.rstudio.com/tags/shinyappsio>". We have created a handy short URL <https://rstd.io/community-shinyappsio> for creating pre-tagged posts.

On September 4th this group will be locked for new posts, but remain in existence to aid in discovering previous answers.

Welcome to the Community!

   -- the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> team
